plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap (greater of 12-month fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), consequential damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-backs, and Excluded Claims in 21.3 covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement. Check mutuality and whether carve-outs are adequate; also note 18.2 (insurance does not limit liability) and 21.4 (independent survival).

No indemnification section appears in the outline (Section 20 is absent although 9.3 cross-references 'Section 20.5' for IP infringement remedies, and 21.3 refers to 'indemnification obligations'). Verify whether an indemnity clause exists anywhere before marking missing; the cross-references suggest a dropped section.

Section 12.4 (second instance) imposes a 24-month worldwide non-compete on Customer covering any competing product or service — squarely against the playbook. Note the direct conflict with 12.3, which states Customer has made no non-compete or exclusivity commitment; cite that inconsistency.

Section 12.3 preserves our freedom to engage any supplier, but 7.2 (first instance) requires disclosure and matching before engaging another provider, which operates as a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal. Treat the matching right under MFN if double-counting is a concern; address exclusivity effect here only if independently breached.

Section 7.2 (first instance) obliges Customer to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer — an MFN running against us, contrary to the direction rule. Section 12.3 disclaims any MFN commitment; flag the conflict.

Section 12.4 (first instance) bars Customer from soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out, unlimited employee scope, one-way. Contrast 12.3, which preserves hiring from general recruitment.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency, and security/service-level termination rights (9.1–9.3, 9.5); no convenience right for Customer appears, and 2.1 expressly denies reduction or termination rights. Confirm absence of a Section 9.4 before concluding missing.

Section 8.2 gives a 30-day non-renewal window plus a 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension; 8.3 caps uplifts at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. Likely compliant — assess against the parametric thresholds rather than assuming deviation.

Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction (outside the accepted list), while 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts — a direct internal conflict. Focus on the Singapore choice-of-law/forum; 28.3 escalation is acceptable.

Section 24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment; 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. Likely compliant and favourable to us — do not flag.

Section 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP (good), but 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence to us — contrary to owning what we pay for. Reconcile with 13.2/14.3 perpetual licence and 6.2 acceptance refunds.

Sections 13.1–13.3 cover Affiliates and contractors, grant a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology, allow transfer, and limit revocation to material uncured breach after notice — largely compliant. The revocable Deliverable licence in 14.2 is the outlier; flag it under IP unless independently breaching this rule.

Section 22 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months with 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, Vendor bears cost unless >5% underpayment, and protects our systems and data. Likely compliant; note Section 23 (records/assurance) has no substantive text in the outline.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer appears; 7.3 bars interest on amounts not due and 27.3 allows fee suspension. The take-or-pay in 2.1 is the closest analogue but belongs under MINCOMMIT — do not double-flag.

Section 19 provides professional-services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, full term for hosted Services), malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties, with repair/re-perform plus termination-and-refund fallback in 19.4 and a non-exclusive remedy carve-out. Likely compliant.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Check limits against playbook thresholds; likely compliant.

Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per-year, three-year take-or-pay with 'no reduction or termination rights' — walk-away territory and inconsistent with 12.3's disclaimer of minimum-volume commitments and with the termination rights in Section 9.

Section 10.1 references an 'agreed transition period' and 10.2 requires delivery of Deliverables and refunds, but no express obligation to return or export Customer Data in a usable format or to provide transition/exit assistance for a defined period. Check 16.5 (return/destroy Confidential Information) and any Section 11 cross-reference before concluding the data-return element is missing.
